claims.claim: The Dragon spacecraft splashed down at 2:03 p.m. PST on November 21 after undocking on November 20 at 11:05 a.m. CST.
claims.episode_span: The unpiloted Dragon spacecraft splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off Southern California at 2:03 p.m. PST on November 21 after undocking from the ISS on November 20 at 11:05 a.m. CST while flying above western China.
claims.source_title: Dragon Returns to Earth Packed With Science and Cargo
claims.supporting_quote: At 2:03 p.m. PST, the unpiloted SpaceX Dragon spacecraft splashed down in the Pacific Ocean near Los Angeles, completing NASA’s 35th SpaceX commercial resupply services mission to the International Space Station.

claims.claim: Dragon returned a 3D-bioprinted blood vessel construct, frozen tumor organoids, microbial samples, and a lighting system tested for more than three years.
claims.episode_span: The capsule returned a 3D-bioprinted blood vessel construct for studies on vascular aging and cardiovascular disease, frozen tumor organoids treated on station that may improve cancer treatments and personalized medicine, frozen microbial samples to examine how antibiotic-resistant bacteria survive and evolve in space, and a lighting system tested for more than three years to support astronaut sleep and well-being on long-duration missions.
claims.source_title: Dragon Returns to Earth Packed With Science and Cargo
claims.supporting_quote: The returning research includes a 3D-bioprinted blood vessel construct used to study vascular aging and cardiovascular disease in space and on Earth. Frozen tumor organoids treated aboard the station also returned and may help researchers identify new ways to improve cancer treatments and advance personalized medicine.

claims.claim: The Falcon 9 launched at 11:20 p.m. EST on November 20 from Vandenberg with booster B1100 on its eleventh flight landing on Of Course I Still Love You.
claims.episode_span: SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 carrying a classified payload for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base at 11:20 p.m. EST on November 20 after a one-day scrub. The booster, designated B1100 and flying its eleventh mission, landed on the droneship Of Course I Still Love You roughly eight and a half minutes after liftoff.
claims.source_title: SpaceX Classified Launch Extends Series Where Space Force Logged 23 Satellites Per Flight
claims.supporting_quote: SpaceX launched the classified USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California at 11:20 p.m. EST on Friday, Nov. 20 (8:20 p.m. local time), and the payload remains undisclosed.

claims.claim: Stainless steel costs roughly 15–20 times less than titanium sheet and gains about 50 percent strength at cryogenic temperatures.
claims.episode_span: At that size the alloy forms and welds far more readily than composites, and its raw-material cost sits roughly fifteen to twenty times lower than equivalent titanium sheet. Cryogenic exposure to liquid oxygen and methane actually raises its yield strength by about fifty percent without the brittleness risk that titanium faces at those temperatures.
claims.source_title: Lift-off with nickel: SpaceX launches mega rocket
claims.supporting_quote: Elon Musk cited several reasons for this change, including lower cost, ease of manufacture, increased strength of stainless steel at cryogenic temperatures, and its ability to withstand high heat.

claims.claim: SpaceX will retire the first Starship upper stage recovered by the tower catch arms rather than fly it again.
